chunks.title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, (1973) 4 SCC 225
chunks.content:
### Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, (1973) 4 SCC 225
**Bench & Court:** 13-Judge Constitution Bench
**Core Holding:** Propounded the Basic Structure Doctrine: Parliament's amending power under Article 368 is not unlimited and cannot alter the foundational features of the Constitution, such as judicial review, rule of law, and democracy.

chunks.title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, AIR 1978 SC 597
chunks.content:
### Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, AIR 1978 SC 597
**Bench & Court:** Supreme Court of India (Bhagwati, J.)
**Core Holding:** Interpreted "procedure established by law" under Article 21 to mean procedure that is just, fair, and reasonable, establishing substantive due process in Indian jurisprudence and interlinking Articles 14, 19, and 21.

chunks.title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 1
chunks.content:
### K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 1
**Bench & Court:** 9-Judge Constitution Bench (Chandrachud, J.)
**Core Holding:** Unanimously affirmed that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right emanating from Article 21 and the freedoms guaranteed under Part III, subject only to proportionality and legitimate state aims.

chunks.title: Procedural Practice Notes — Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction
chunks.content: # Procedural Practice Notes — Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction

chunks.title: Scope of Judicial Review & Locus Standi
chunks.content:
### Scope of Judicial Review & Locus Standi
1. **Writ Guidelines:** Writs lie against "State" under Article 12 or bodies discharging public functions.
2. **Proportionality Doctrine:** State restrictions on fundamental rights must satisfy the 4-prong proportionality test (legitimate aim, suitability, necessity, and strict balancing).

chunks.title: Constitution of India — Fundamental Rights (Part III)
chunks.content:
### Constitution of India — Fundamental Rights (Part III)
- **Article 14:** Equality before the law and equal protection of the laws; prohibition of arbitrariness in State action.
- **Article 19(1)(a)-(g):** Fundamental freedoms (speech, peaceful assembly, association, movement, residence, profession) subject to reasonable restrictions under Art 19(2)-(6).
- **Article 21:** Protection of life and personal liberty; right to fair trial, bodily integrity, dignified livelihood, and privacy.
- **Article 32 & 226:** Constitutional remedies — Power of Supreme Court and High Courts to issue writs of Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari for enforcement of fundamental and legal rights.
